questions.stem_text:
Suppose your model is overfitting. Which of the following is NOT a valid way to try and
reduce the overfitting?

options.A: Increase the amount of training data.
options.B: Improve the optimisation algorithm being used for error minimisation.
options.D: Reduce the noise in the training data.

questions.answer_explanation: Improving the optimization algorithm primarily affects the convergence speed and efficiency of training rather than directly addressing the model's complexity and its tendency to overfit the training data.

questions.stem_text: Out-of-distribution detection is also referred to as anomaly detection in machine learning.
questions.answer_explanation: Out-of-distribution detection is considered a form of anomaly detection because both involve identifying data points that significantly deviate from the expected distribution, indicating they are unusual or not representative of the normal dataset.

questions.stem_text: The number of test examples needed for statistically significant results is larger if the error rate is smaller.
questions.answer_explanation: A smaller error rate implies that the model is performing better, requiring a larger sample size to reliably distinguish between the subtle differences in performance and to ensure that the observed results are not due to random chance.
